ARTICLE: AI FOR FINANCIAL MARKETING, PART 1 — COMPLIANCE
Published: October 4, 2024 | rainlocal.com/post/ai-for-financial-marketing

AI technologies are exploding in financial marketing. Key capabilities include:
transcribing video calls with summaries, analyzing complex databases using natural
language, and custom AI tools for specific workflows.

MOST COMMON CLIENT QUESTION: COMPLIANCE
The AI topic bank and credit union clients ask about most frequently is compliance.
Two questions RAIN hears constantly:

Q: Does AI-enabled audience segmentation break fair lending laws by excluding demographics?
A (from RAIN): No. Financial marketing tools reach broad audiences. As audiences interact
with campaigns, AI helps optimize by retargeting users who have shown interest.
AI optimizes toward engagement — it does not exclude protected classes.

Q: Does collecting consumer data with AI tools put financial institutions at risk
for noncompliance with consumer privacy rules?
A (from RAIN): No. All mainstream AI marketing tools anonymize individual data,
so individuals cannot be identified even if someone wanted to.

THE DEEPER CONCERN:
These questions are really about trust. Financial institutions want to know they
can trust their marketing partners when it comes to emerging technologies.

RAIN'S VIEW: "Financial marketing teams are compliance teams."
The finance industry has strict rules to keep customer data from being used in
harmful or predatory ways. Banks and credit unions trust external partners to
prioritize compliance even above other work.

RAIN's Head of Sales James McCool:
"Yes, of course, RAIN is utilizing cutting-edge AI solutions wherever we can to
make our operations more efficient and effective, but we're doing it carefully.
We promise to take every precaution with every AI tool we use, ensuring no
compliance guidelines are broken and no risks are taken."

RAIN'S TWO GUIDING PRINCIPLES FOR EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES:

1. Discernment: Stay informed — not just about what technologies can do, but how
   they work and what industry experts say. While AI excels at data processing speed,
   humans have intimate knowledge of the finance industry rooted in experience.

2. Transparency: RAIN is open with clients about where and how AI tools are used
   to support campaigns. RAIN is not using generative AI to "fill in the gaps."

"We're making sure humans are the final word for process design, guidance,
testing and approval." — RAIN team

ARTICLE: THE DIGITAL MARKETING PLAYBOOK FOR BANKS AND CREDIT UNIONS
Published: September 30, 2025 | rainlocal.com/post/digital-marketing-playbook-for-banks-credit-unions

FIVE KEY ELEMENTS OF A SUCCESSFUL FINANCIAL MARKETING STRATEGY:

1. INVEST IN A STRONG FOUNDATION
   - Mobile-first, conversion-optimized landing pages
   - Tag every meaningful interaction (button clicks, form starts, calculators)
   - Integrate into application portal when possible to track end-to-end
   - Right tech stack: GTM, GA4, CRM integrations — measurable, auditable, future-ready

2. MATCH GOALS TO CHANNELS
   Every channel has a specific job:
   - Awareness: Display, Video, Social, Programmatic/CTV
   - Consideration: SEO, Organic Social, Retargeting
   - Conversion: Search Ads (Google/Bing), Cross-channel retargeting, Email/SMS

3. DESIGN CREATIVE THAT CONNECTS
   - Take inventory of existing assets — find what works and why
   - Focus on relevance and storytelling — use real people and real customer scenarios
   - Refresh regularly — creative fatigue sets in fast (2 months for display)
   - Use benchmark data to identify formats that perform best per platform
   - Compliance is baked into creative strategy, not an afterthought

4. REFINE TARGETING WITH DATA
   - Special Ad Category rules limit some demographic targeting for financial products
   - First-party data is powerful: CRM lists, email subscribers, retargeting pools
   - Best approach: blend first-party data with platform targeting capabilities
   - Cross-channel retargeting (video + display + search) multiplies results

5. MEASURE AND REPORT THE RIGHT KPIs
   Most valuable KPIs connect to business goals:
   - Macro KPIs: New account openings, loan applications, deposits opened, CPA
   - Supporting metrics: Conversion rates, engagement, frequency, bounce rates

EXAMPLE — DEPOSIT GROWTH GOAL:
   If goal is to grow deposits by $50M:
   - Set up GA4 conversion tracking for account openings
   - Awareness campaigns: Display, video, social, community sponsorships
   - Consideration: Landing page content + search ads for "high-yield savings", "CD rates"
   - Conversion: Cross-channel retargeting, email/SMS to existing customers
   - Measure: Cost per depositor, account openings, balance velocity

RAIN's philosophy:
"It isn't about running a perfect campaign or trying to go viral; it's about
creating a system that consistently works to grow your institution in real,
material ways, regardless of a constantly shifting digital marketing environment."

"You do not rise to the level of your goals. You fall to the level of your systems."
— James Clear (quoted by RAIN)

CASE STUDY 1: LA CAPITOL FEDERAL CREDIT UNION
Bump Rate Share Certificate Campaign
Source: rainlocal.com/case-studies/la-cap

RESULTS AT A GLANCE:
- 1.47 million impressions
- 14,400 clicks
- 0.98% click-through rate (CTR)
- 639% increase in website traffic during the 45-day campaign
- 678 new Bump Rate Share Certificate accounts opened
- $34.3 million in deposits generated
- Over half of all new accounts came from non-members (new customer acquisition)
- Most accounts opened by consumers aged 51–88

THE CHALLENGE:
La Capitol Federal Credit Union was facing a growing loan-to-deposit ratio after
three years of low interest rates. Coupled with rapidly rising federal fund rates,
the credit union needed to increase deposits to maintain balance and support
continued growth. The goal was to increase Bump Rate Share Certificate account openings.

RAIN'S APPROACH — "THE RIGHT" FRAMEWORK:

The Right Product:
The Bump Rate Share Certificate was the ideal product to promote in August and
September amid rising interest rates and market uncertainty, when consumers seek
stable, predictable financial options.

The Right Time:
The 45-day campaign budget was strategically weighted, with more spend allocated
following the anticipated Federal Reserve rate announcement.

The Right People:
Bump Rate Share Certificates are popular among older and more financially
conservative consumers. Targeting focused on this demographic.

The Right Place:
Heavy emphasis was placed on in-app mobile advertising, targeting specific
demographics to reach the highest potential consumers. Retargeting was performed
on both mobile and website visitors. Certain landing pages were retargeted to
cross-sell to existing members.

Geographic strategy: Initially targeted areas near branches in Louisiana.
15 days into the campaign, targeting was expanded to include all of Louisiana
and selected cities in Texas, Mississippi, and Florida — chosen for proximity
to main service areas and desired demographics.

The Right Creatives:
Many financial institutions were promoting share certificates at the same time,
so La Capitol needed to stand out. RAIN developed the tagline "Time to Grow
Your Savings" paired with imagery of being on a mountain top with open arms —
reinforcing the accomplishment of opening an account. Interest rates and
call-to-action buttons were prominently displayed without detracting from the
overall message. The traditional brand color palette was slightly modified to
stronger shades.

KEY TAKEAWAYS FROM THIS CAMPAIGN:
1. Timing campaigns around anticipated market events (Fed rate announcements) maximizes impact
2. Expanding geographic targeting mid-campaign based on early performance data improves results
3. Differentiated creative is critical when many competitors are promoting similar products
4. Mobile-first targeting reaches the right audience effectively
5. Over half of new accounts came from non-members — showing digital ads reach beyond existing members
6. $34.3M in deposits from one 45-day campaign demonstrates measurable ROI of digital marketing

CASE STUDY 2: MID-SIZE REGIONAL BANK HIRING CAMPAIGN
Source: rainlocal.com/case-studies/regional-bank-hiring-campaign

RESULTS AT A GLANCE:
- 161% surge in job applications
- 31% rise in new hires
- 1,089,887 impressions
- 19,452 clicks
- 1.78% click-through rate (CTR)
- 9,681 total applications received (vs 3,707 the prior year — same period)
- 328 new external hires made (vs 249 the prior year) — despite 3% fewer open positions

THE CHALLENGE:
A regional bank was struggling to attract high-quality applicants for open positions.
Traditional job boards like Indeed were only capturing candidates at the bottom of
the funnel, leaving a wealth of untapped potential at the top of the funnel.
Goal: Bring in qualified job applicants relevant to the open positions.

RAIN'S APPROACH:
RAIN took a proactive approach that went beyond conventional job boards.
RAIN used smart targeting on Facebook, Instagram, and Google to identify and
engage potential candidates who would be an excellent fit.

The multi-layered campaign used:
- Demographic data targeting
- Behavioral insights
- Keyword targeting
Goal: Reach a more qualified and diverse audience

RAIN also optimized ad creatives and landing pages to ensure a seamless and
compelling user experience. This captured candidates at various stages of the
job-seeking process — including valuable prospects at the top of the funnel who
may not have been actively looking but were the right fit for the roles.

KEY TAKEAWAYS FROM THIS CAMPAIGN:
1. Social and search advertising reaches passive job seekers that job boards miss
2. Multi-layered targeting (demographic + behavioral + keyword) improves candidate quality
3. Optimizing the application landing page reduces drop-off and improves completion rates
4. RAIN's targeting capabilities extend beyond customer acquisition into talent acquisition
5. 161% more applications with the same targeting approach used for customer campaigns

RAIN AGENCY — SERVICES
Source: rainlocal.com

RAIN offers four core service areas to its clients:


1. DIGITAL ADVERTISING

RAIN creates and manages digital ad campaigns across multiple platforms to find
new customers and convert those already familiar with the brand.

Channels RAIN runs:
- Display advertising
- Social media advertising (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn)
- Paid search (Google, Bing)
- Video advertising (YouTube, social video)
- Connected TV (CTV) — streaming platforms like Hulu
- App and desktop display advertising with ultra-precise geotargeting

RAIN's approach: Tailor time-perfected strategies to each business's goals.
RAIN looks at the product, website, audience, and budget to find the most
cost-effective combination of platforms. Campaigns balance reach, efficiency,
and compliance.

For financial institutions specifically, RAIN runs:
- Social media ads to reach consumers where they spend 2.5 hours each day
- Paid search to make it simple for interested prospects to find the institution
- App and desktop display with precise geotargeting and placement on popular apps and sites
- Programmatic/CTV for targeted reach in defined geographies, useful for CRA objectives


2. CREATIVE MEDIA STRATEGY

RAIN's full-service in-house creative team is what sets them apart.
After analyzing countless campaigns' performance data, RAIN knows what works.

Creative formats RAIN produces:
- Static ads
- Video ads
- Animated ads
- Audio ads

RAIN relies on benchmark data to identify creative types, formats, and messages
that perform best across each platform. All creative is designed to be:
- Aligned with the client's brand
- Refreshed regularly (creative fatigue sets in fast)
- Fully compliant with financial regulations at every step

RAIN's principle on compliance and creative:
"Compliance should not be thought of as an annoying checkbox or an afterthought;
rather, it's something we bake into our creative strategy."

Creative refresh guidance: RAIN finds 2 months is a good rule of thumb for
display campaigns, anchored to ad frequency, reach, and performance decay per channel.


3. WEB OPTIMIZATION

RAIN's job isn't over when traffic starts flowing in. RAIN helps improve
engagement and conversion rates for all traffic — not just from their ads.

Web optimization services include:
- Landing page recommendations and optimization
- UX/UI design improvements
- Application journey analysis and optimization

RAIN's approach to landing pages: Every landing page action is tagged with a
three-tier conversion system based on the user's level of intent. These categories
allow RAIN to optimize campaigns more effectively and provide high-value reporting.

Key principle: Integrate into the application portal when possible to track
outcomes end-to-end. This often requires vendor cooperation and cross-domain linking.

Mobile-first is non-negotiable: Most users — including Baby Boomers — now engage
with financial institutions on phones first. All creative, landing pages, and
experiences must be designed with mobile devices in mind.


4. REPORTS AND DASHBOARD

RAIN ensures full measurement and transparency for every campaign.

Reporting services:
- GTM (Google Tag Manager) and GA4 (Google Analytics 4) conversion tracking setup
- Periodic performance reporting (monthly reports)
- Interactive real-time dashboard (clients can browse data themselves)

RAIN's reporting process:
Before launching anything, RAIN ensures GTM and GA4 are set up correctly.
Then RAIN performs extensive performance analysis daily to ensure campaign goals are met.
Clients can browse their own data via an interactive reporting dashboard.

Tools RAIN uses:
- Google Tag Manager (GTM) — tag management
- Google Analytics 4 (GA4) — conversion tracking and analytics
- Datorama — unified campaign reporting dashboard
- Looker Studio — client-facing interactive dashboards

RAIN's three-tier conversion tracking system:
RAIN tags all landing page actions by user intent level:
- Tier 1 (high intent): Application submitted, account opened, Apply Now clicked
- Tier 2 (medium intent): Application started, calculator used, Learn More clicked
- Tier 3 (low intent): Homepage visit, blog read, product page viewed
This system allows RAIN to optimize toward the highest-value actions and
provide granular reporting including census-tract level data for CRA compliance.

RAIN'S DIGITAL MARKETING STRATEGY FRAMEWORK

RAIN uses a three-stage funnel approach matching channels to campaign goals:

AWARENESS AND BRAND TRUST (top of funnel):
- Display and Video Ads: Top and mid-funnel visibility
- Social Media Ads: Full-funnel if used correctly, great for awareness
- Programmatic/CTV: Targeted reach in defined geographies, useful for CRA objectives

CONSIDERATION AND ENGAGEMENT (mid funnel):
- Website Optimization/SEO: Always-on foundation for discoverability
- Organic Social Media: Build community engagement and reputation

CONVERSION (bottom of funnel):
- Search Ads (Google and Bing): Captures high-intent prospects actively searching
  Examples: "best HELOC rates near me", "open checking account online"
- Cross-channel retargeting: Display and social following website visits
- Email, SMS, In-app notifications: Direct lines to existing customers for cross-sell

RAIN's principle: A checking campaign behaves differently than a mortgage or CD campaign.
RAIN looks at the product, website, audience, and budget to build a multi-channel
campaign that balances reach, efficiency, and compliance.

AUDIENCE TARGETING APPROACH:
First-party data (most precise):
- CRM lists from client
- Email subscriber lists
- Website retargeting pools via pixel
- Limitation: lists must be large to scale; repeated use causes ad fatigue

Best practice: Blend first-party data with platform targeting capabilities.
Cross-channel retargeting multiplies results synergistically.
